intent.quote: I fear that there are actually many duplicates, or that the actual definition of an SR is actually blur currently in the plumb project.
intent.readback: What the records say is the only specification, so plumb keeps the repository free of what the records have replaced. When work lands, the documents its records supersede and the working files it used are removed, and log entries older than the records they served are folded into one archive segment per kind that validate still checks but a session start never reads. A tidy job at each merge into main keeps it that way, so you never clean up by hand.
will: Remove, at each merge into main, the documents the landed records supersede and the working files of the landed work, as the landing names them.
Compact log entries older than the records they served into one archive segment per kind; validate still checks the chain through the segments; a session start never reads them.
Run the tidy job at the merge in the background and say in the plumb line what it removed and compacted.
For the version 2 landing: delete the sub-project specs and plans of sub-projects 1 to 8 and followups.md, compact the logs, and remove the v2 working files and the pruned-worktree archive.
wont: Delete a log entry outright: compacted entries keep their digests and chain inside the archive segment.
Remove a document or file no landing named as superseded or as a working file, or one a current record still cites unless the landing first rewords that record.
Ask you which files to remove or have you read a list to approve: whether a document is superseded is the AI's judgement (P3, P5 addendum).
Delete sp9-intent-loop.md or other documents outside sub-projects 1 to 8 in the v2 landing, unless a later landing names them.
Compact on a branch: only main's tidy job writes archive segments, so segments never conflict in a merge.
assumptions: The agent writes, in the landing, the list of superseded documents and working files to remove; the owner types no path or id (P2).

"Older than the records they served": an entry is archived when every record it names has since been superseded, retired or changed (its hash moved on), or, for test-run evidence, when a newer run covers the same tests; an entry naming no record is archived once it is older than the previous landing.
Removed documents stay in git history; code comments citing them (e.g. "spec 5.7", "SP6 6") are rewritten to the records that replaced them when that code is next touched, not in a sweep.
The pruned-worktree archive (C:/coding/plumb-wt/_archive-2026-10-16-worktree-untracked/) lies outside the repository; it is removed once, in the v2 landing, because the owner named it.

No old cluster or record is governed by P15, so these requirements supersede nothing and implemented_by is empty; the code they will touch is likely src/plumb/log.py, src/plumb/validate.py, src/plumb/merge.py, src/plumb/logcmd.py and src/plumb/paths.py.
A failure of the tidy job goes to the debug workflow (P5); the merge's hold stays for intent only (P11).

requirements.title: Each merge into main tidies away what the landed records supersede
requirements.statement: When work merges into main, a background tidy job deletes, in one tidy commit, the documents the landed records supersede and the working files the landing names (the landing lists those paths in its decision record), and removes any named folder outside the repository without a commit. A file a current record still cites is kept, unless the landing first rewords that record to cite the records that replaced the document; for the version 2 landing that means the descriptions and 'Sub-project N' titles of FEAT-001 to FEAT-008. The plumb line of the first turn end after the job finishes names what was removed; running it again changes nothing.

examples.given: the version 2 records land, their decision record names the sub-project specs and plans of sub-projects 1 to 8, followups.md and the v2 working files, and the landing rewords the FEAT-001 to FEAT-008 descriptions and titles that cite those specs and plans
examples.then: those files are gone in the landing's tidy commit, sp9-intent-loop.md and concept.md stay, no current record cites a removed file, and the next turn end's plumb line names what was removed

examples.given: the version 2 landing also names the pruned-worktree archive, a folder outside the repository
examples.then: the folder is removed without any commit, and the same plumb line names it

examples.given: a landing names as superseded a document that a current confirmed record still cites
examples.then: the document stays and the inconsistency goes to the debug workflow, not to the owner

examples.given: the tidy job already ran for this landing
examples.then: no file is deleted, written or committed

examples.given: an owner's file in docs/ that no landing named

proof.plan: Recommended: on the version 2 landing, the owner sees the plumb line naming what was removed, the agent shows the tidy commit's file list matching it, and running the tidy job again reports nothing to do. The owner decides whether this is the proof.

requirements.title: Old log entries are compacted into one archive segment per kind
requirements.statement: At a merge into main the tidy job moves into one archive segment per kind every log entry older than the records it served: an entry all of whose named records have since been superseded, retired or changed; test-run evidence a newer run of the same tests replaces; and an entry naming no record that is older than the previous landing. Each entry keeps its digest and prev; validate checks the chain through the segments and reports any change inside them. A session start never reads a segment; calibration, the judge jobs, verify and explain read through them as they read live entries.

examples.given: about 7,800 judgment entries, most of them about records the version 2 landing superseded
examples.when: the tidy job compacts the log
examples.then: the entries about superseded records sit in the judgment kind's archive segment, the ones about current records stay as entry files, and plumb validate is clean

examples.given: a live entry whose prev names an entry now in an archive segment
examples.then: the prev resolves in the segment and no chain break is reported

examples.given: an entry inside an archive segment edited by hand
examples.then: it reports the kind, the segment and the entry whose digest no longer matches
the brief and the hooks read only live entry files and open no archive segment

examples.given: test-run evidence that makes a current test fresh
examples.when: the tidy job compacts the log
examples.then: that evidence stays live and plumb verify keeps the test fresh

examples.given: a branch created before the compaction that appended entries chained onto now-archived ones
examples.then: git merges without conflict and plumb validate is clean

examples.given: the agent asks why a retired record was retired
examples.then: the answer reads the archive segment for the entries that record the retirement

examples.given: the log was already compacted for this landing
examples.then: no segment or entry file changes

examples.given: test-run evidence for a test that a newer run of the same test has replaced
examples.when: the tidy job compacts the log
examples.then: the older evidence moves to the evidence kind's segment and the newer one stays live

examples.given: a merge-evidence entry naming no record, older than the previous landing
examples.when: the tidy job compacts the log
examples.then: it moves to its kind's segment

examples.given: an approval of a current record, and the prompt entry its pre-intent names
examples.when: the tidy job compacts the log
examples.then: both stay live as entry files

examples.given: an approval of a record the landing superseded
examples.when: the tidy job compacts the log, and the agent then asks plumb explain about that record
examples.then: the approval moves to the approval kind's segment and the explanation still names who approved the record and when

examples.given: the owner's labelled answers and reversals, some about records the landing superseded
examples.when: calibration runs before and after the compaction
examples.then: it counts the same labelled set, with the same number of 'no' examples, both times

proof.plan: Recommended: show the entry counts per kind before and after the version 2 compaction, a clean plumb validate, and a session-start trace of the files read with no archive segment among them. The owner decides whether this is the proof.

decisions.question: What does the version 2 landing remove from the repository?
decisions.chosen: Delete the sub-project specs and plans of sub-projects 1 to 8 and followups.md, compact the logs, and remove the v2 working files and the pruned-worktree archive after landing.
alternatives: Keep the old specs and plans beside the records as background reading.
Leave the log uncompacted and let the session-start read keep growing.
